einzeiler: The 2009 murder of D.C. restaurateur Nori Amaya remains unsolved despite DNA and video.
kurzfassung: On Halloween night in 2009, 38-year-old Nori Amaya went dancing, returned home, and was found strangled in her apartment two days later. Investigators gathered surveillance footage and unknown male DNA, but widespread costumes and missing items complicated the case. Her family continues to seek answers, believing someone in her inner circle knows the truth.
stichpunkte: Nori Amaya was discovered strangled and beaten in her bed on November 2, 2009.
Her apartment door was locked with no signs of forced entry, and her purse was left untouched.
An autopsy revealed physical trauma and sexual assault, along with unknown male touch DNA.
The killer cut and removed Nori's fingernails and took her small red digital camera.
Nori spent Halloween night at a Latin club owned by Gustavo, a married man she was seeing.
Police tested DNA from Gustavo, his wife, a former employee, and a longtime friend named David, but found no matches.
An exterminator who visited the building on Monday may have locked the apartment door after the murder.
Investigators and family believe genetic genealogy or a tip from someone in Nori's circle could finally solve the case.

clips.hook: The killer took the time to cut and remove her fingernails.
clips.text: The perpetrator systematically cut down and removed the victim's long fingernails from the crime scene to eliminate potential evidence.

clips.hook: An apartment complex of over 1,100 units is basically a small city.
clips.text: The building where the crime occurred was massive, housing more than a thousand units across 12 floors.

clips.hook: Detectives flew to South America on an undercover spy mission.
clips.text: Investigators traveled internationally and went undercover to covertly obtain a suspect's DNA from drinking glasses.

clips.hook: She often left her door unlocked because the building felt safe.
clips.text: The victim frequently relied on the building's multi-layered security and chose not to lock her apartment door.

clips.hook: The entire population of the host's childhood town lived in that building.
clips.text: The sheer number of residents in the apartment complex rivaled the size of an entire small town.

beschreibung:
On Halloween night in 2009, 38-year-old D.C. restaurateur and salsa queen Nori Amaya went out dancing, came home alone, and was found strangled in her bed two days later. Police have DNA and hours of surveillance footage, but in a building full of people in Halloween masks, they've never been able to identify her killer. Sixteen years later, the key to solving this case could be a secret someone in Nori's world is still keeping, or something that went missing from her apartment the night she died.
If you have any information about the murder of Nori Amaya, please call the Metropolitan Police Department of District of Columbia at 202-727-9099, or you can reach us by e-mailing tips@audiochuck.com.
